whatItFakes: Business-day windows skip weekends but not legal holidays.
why: The old action-window loop has no holiday input.
replacement: Caller-selected holiday calendar admitted for the jurisdiction and year.

whatItFakes: Always returns null for inaction outcome after adjournment.
why: The old helper calculates the deadline but does not resolve the after-adjournment legal outcome.
replacement: Dated after-adjournment inaction provisions; CTO decides the change.

whatItFakes: Caps the fractional vote requirement at the denominator, including zero members.

replacement: CTO-approved empty-body/quorum interpretation and equivalence change.

whatItFakes: Deals recorded seniority order around committees in compiled order.
why: Authored gameplay profile substitutes for actual committee appointment decisions.
replacement: Saved appointment decisions under each body's procedure.

whatItFakes: Subtracts 1e-9 before ceiling a fractional vote requirement.
replacement: Exact rational vote arithmetic with a reviewed rounding contract.

whatItFakes: Searches at most twice through the member order per committee.
why: Preserve the legacy defensive guard, including any underfilled result.
replacement: Validated member uniqueness and a proven complete roster operation.

whatItFakes: Searches only through the year four years after the starting year.
why: A later eligible sitting can be rejected by the legacy bound.
replacement: Validated recurrence bounds or unbounded direct calculation.

whatItFakes: Matter-bearing council items remain pending and playedMeasureIds is always empty.

replacement: Core2 council scene/effect consumer recording actual played items.

whatItFakes: Authored fractional or negative disposition counts are not validated and can disagree with the reported total.
why: Preserve the unchanged legacy behavior while lifting only its pure decision kernel.
replacement: Reviewed integer, nonnegative, bounded vote-count input contract.

whatItFakes: Congressional review counts every weekday, omitting holidays and Congress recess exclusions.
why: Preserve the unchanged legacy behavior while lifting only its pure decision kernel.
replacement: Supplied lawful review calendar with holidays and applicable recess intervals.
